title: Pictures must not misplace a quoted line
statement: A picture beside a quotation must not imply the line is spoken, or a character present, where the text doesn't place them, and notes record where each quotation comes from.
detail: The 6 October handover found that the Grade 9 opening's optional quotation pin belongs to a reunion in a later act, set in another place than the illustration beside it; it calls that picture not a literal depiction of the speech and asks for the distinction to be kept clear in source notes and visual review (line 168). The film treatment asks for cuts to be revised if they imply a character is present in a scene where the play does not place them (`g9/film/TREATMENT.md`, line 30). The later film labels the quotation with its act and scene on screen and sets the early quotation and the late event as the two ends of one line (`g9/film/v07/plates.json`, line 28; `g9/film/v07/storyboard-v7.json`, line 243).

evidence.quote: A relationship illustration set in Venice is not a literal depiction of that speech. Keep this distinction clear in source notes and visual review.
Character identity and setting must be checked during academic and visual review; the final cuts should be revised if they imply a character is present in a scene where the play does not place them.
The A-to-B line: the 2.1 quote at A, the 5.2 fact at B
